title: Facts: what GitHub holds about one pull request, read in one pass. No prose.

characters.description: How long the whole diff is as a Task carries it, escaped as JSON, counted from the bytes the content id is the digest of. Absent where GitHub would not serve the diff or its bytes are no UTF-8, which no Task carries; a pull request whose count is absent or past the configuration's max_diff_characters is held too large (issue 327)

changed_paths.description: One record for each file the pull request changes, as many as the diff has files, each by its own path once, from the top of the repo: `previous` is the path a renamed or copied file had before, and null for any other change. A name is never empty, . or .., so no path starts or ends with / or holds //. The Kernel matches every path and every previous one against the configuration's protected paths and Lenses' inputs, and never shows one

label_events.description: Every labeled and unlabeled event on the pull request's timeline, with who added or removed the label and when, read with the timeline, so complete.timeline says whether they were read in full. The port's contract: it gives them as the timeline lists them. The Kernel reads them by time; in the same second it reads each label the way that stops work: a Hold stands, an admission does not, and hands-off a person removed in that second is read as a Hold; a removal by anyone else ends nothing, then or later. A control label binds from when anyone adds it until a person removes it, and anyone else placing it again does not replace a person's placement; hands-off and an admission bind as a person's only when a person placed them

last_reopened_at.description: When the pull request was last reopened, from its timeline's `reopened` event (trials/P-7.reopened.json), or null if it never was. An approval submitted before it does not stand (issue 378)

state.description: As GitHub holds it now: a review that was dismissed is dismissed, whatever it said.

dismissed_by.description: Who dismissed the review, from the timeline; null unless it was dismissed.

dismissed_from.description: What a dismissed review was before, from the timeline (previousReviewState); null unless it was dismissed.

category.description: The Finding's category, as the authority table names it: a person's thread is human. A required Lens's, and its severity, come from its own Finding record joined by surface.key, never the comment text; null there is unreadable. Null for a Lens that writes it only as prose. A security Finding gates at any severity

resolved_by.description: Who resolved the thread, of what kind and with what access; null unless it is resolved. A person's thread resolved by anyone but that person stays open, and a Lens's resolved by anyone but that Lens's App or a person

name.description: The check run's name exactly as GitHub gives it. The port's contract: it gives every check run on the head with its exact name and the id of the App that really reported it, from every App, and never drops, merges or renames one. The Kernel matches a check to a required deterministic Lens by the Lens's `check` in the configuration, exactly. Only a re-run of the same job in the same check suite replaces an earlier run (GitHub's filter=latest is per check suite), so two workflow runs on one commit both stay, and both are read

app_id.description: The id of the App that reported the check, as GitHub gives it: the check run's app.id. A required Lens is read only from the App the configuration names for it

workflow.description: The path of the workflow file that ran the check, as GitHub gives it for the workflow run of the check run's check suite (its `path`, such as .github/workflows/verify.yml), passed on verbatim, a dynamic/ one too; null only for a check no workflow ran, as one GitHub Advanced Security reports. GitHub Actions is one App for every job in the repo, so a required Lens that it runs is read only from the path the configuration names for it. The path is text from outside: a Decision shows it only in the configuration's form

conclusion.description: GitHub's own conclusion, or the check's status while it has not concluded. The port maps nothing; config check_conclusions says what each means.

completed_at.description: When the check completed, as GitHub says; null while it has not. An item's wait counts from the newest time it moved

acceptance.description: The item's acceptance contract (design §3.13, §4.8), as the Kernel reads it: null when the issue the pull request closes asks for none, read from that issue and never from the head, which only a full read (complete.acceptance) confirms. `approved` is the contract a person approved, read at the commit of the newest approving review by a person, or null where none has; `head` is the contract's digest at the head, or null where the head carries none. A digest covers the contract and every path it protects, so an edit to a test it names changes it. A contract no person approved, or whose head differs from what was approved, is a Hold, read before anything admits a Run (I-29). Each result is one read for one criterion, from the check that gave it, with the content_id of the content it ran on; the port's contract is the latest result per criterion per check suite. Only this content's results are judged, and only from the Lens the configuration's acceptance_reporters names for the criterion's kind: a result from any other check, App or workflow file is unreadable, and so is any result for a kind no Lens reports. A criterion of kind human is passed only by a person's undismissed approval of this content. A contract, or a result on this content, that the Kernel cannot read converges nothing and admits nothing

approved.description: The contract a person approved: its digest, who approved it, and its criteria, each by id and kind, never their statements; null where no person has approved one. Its criteria are the contract's: the head's are never read

commit.description: The commit the approving review was given on, as the review gives it: the Kernel holds the approval to a review in `reviews` by that person, on that commit, approving, and not dismissed by a person

criteria.description: Each criterion of the approved contract, by its id, each once, and the kind of its check, as schemas/acceptance.schema.json names them

head.description: The digest of the contract and every path it protects at the head, or null where the head carries no contract: a deleted contract is a change, never no contract

check.description: The check that reported the result, as the facts give a check: its name exactly as GitHub gives it, the id of the App that reported it, and the path of the workflow file that ran it, null for a check no workflow ran

acceptance.description: Whether the four reads of the acceptance contract were read in full: whether the linked issue asks for one, the contract a person approved, its digest at the head, and every result for it

changed_paths.description: Whether every path the pull request changes was read: a list paged, or cut off at its limit, says no

timeline.description: Whether the timeline was read in full: the one read behind both acts_since_writer and label_events

actor.description: Who acted, of what kind, and whether they have write access: who submitted a review, opened a thread, or added or removed a label

actor_kind.description: The port's contract: it tells the kind from GitHub's own account type and the configuration, never from a name's spelling (I-28, L-57). human: a User account. machine_user: the User the configuration names as the approver, and no other. lens: the Bot account of an App that reports as a Lens, a Role's or a third-party reviewer's. app: the Bot account of any other App. A person is human with write access, read with one named credential; nobody else is

time.description: UTC, to the second, each field in its range. That the day is one its month has, the Kernel checks

digest.description: An acceptance contract's digest, over the contract and every path it protects: sha256: and a whole SHA-256 in lower-case hexadecimal, never cut short
